facts.title: A tronie that became an icon
facts.body: Vermeer’s Girl with a Pearl Earring (c. 1665) is a tronie — a character study, not a named portrait. The Mauritshuis panel is famous for its turban, moist glance, and a pearl that may be glass or invention.

facts.title: An unknown sitter
facts.body: No document names her. She exists as light on cheek and wetness in the eye — presence without biography.

facts.title: A pearl too large to be real
facts.body: The earring’s scale suggests glass, tin, or pure painterly invention. Vermeer builds it from a few bright strokes.

facts.title: Exotic cloth, Dutch light
facts.body: The blue-and-yellow turban was fashionable orientalizing costume in Dutch tronies — foreign fabric under northern window light.

facts.title: Caught turning
facts.body: She turns as if we just spoke. The glance invents a relationship in a single instant.

facts.title: A mouth about to answer
facts.body: Slightly parted lips catch a highlight — breath made visible.

facts.title: Black that was green
facts.body: The background was once a warm green glaze over black; age darkened it into the void we know.

facts.title: A yellow wrap
facts.body: The jacket’s ochre folds ground the floating head in cloth and weight.
